title: Separating QUF from QAE
summary: The source notes that QAE implies cQCA and leaves open whether the proposed construction exists to separate QUF from QAE.

formal_statement.body: Does there exist a symmetric-key quantum encryption scheme that satisfies $\mathrm{QUF}$ but not $\mathrm{QAE}$, thereby proving $\mathrm{QUF}\not\Rightarrow\mathrm{QAE}$?

scope.domain: This concerns symmetric-key quantum encryption and relationships among quantum security notions.
parameters: QUF and QAE, the security notions whose implication is being tested
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the scheme discussed below Proposition 4 exists and proves that QUF does not imply QAE.

progress.summary: The paper lists this explicitly in the Discussion as an open question about the encryption scheme discussed below Proposition 4. The proposed route uses a one-time scheme with cQCA security for trivial adversarial side information but insecurity with nontrivial side information, followed by a PRF; existence of that base scheme remains open.
citation_labels: Gorjan Alagic et al., Unforgeable Quantum Encryption
